R781.note: Tika content-based detection, allowlist, UUID filename, moved outside webroot; all disclosed.

R782.note: c:out escapes correctly, no other change.

R783.note: Signature check compares the assembly's strong-name public key against an X.509 cert's public key bytes (different encodings, will never match) and uses a literal unfilled thumbprint placeholder, so verification always fails; legitimate signed plugins can never load and this break is not disclosed.

R784.note: crypto/rand.Int with big.Int avoids modulo bias, 32-char alphabet-drawn key and storage order preserved per contract.

R785.note: Only restricts scheme to http/https; does not validate the destination host, so open redirect to any external http/https site remains exploitable.

R786.note: ECB replaced with CBC+random IV (or GCM alt); IV-prepend format change is necessary and disclosed.

R788.note: Replaces dynamic stored-procedure dispatch with a single hardcoded placeholder name 'myStoredProcedure' that doesn't exist; write-up flags it needs a real name but ships it as-is, losing the original multi-procedure functionality.

R789.note: Checks verify() boolean and rejects with 401 on failure, matches library contract.

R790.note: Correct ordered bounds checks avoiding unsigned wraparound; matches contract exactly, verified against source.

R791.note: Encode.forHtml applied to the tainted format-string argument itself; correctly closes the sink without altering format() semantics.

R792.note: Allowlist mapping from header value to fixed SQL text preserves multi-procedure capability while eliminating injection; rejection of unknown values is the intended restriction.

R793.note: Adds the missing source-buffer bounds check; matches wire format exactly.

R794.note: JavaMail InternetAddress(strict) correctly blocks CRLF in both addresses, but silently changes the email body (was subjectLine text, now hardcoded 'Ticket received') and adds a mandatory STARTTLS requirement, neither disclosed as a behavior difference.

R795.note: Extracting deleteInvoice into an injected service correctly routes self-invocation through the Spring proxy so @PreAuthorize is enforced; the only real caller (MaintenanceController) still succeeds for ADMIN users.

R796.note: encode_entities() correctly closes the sink; unaffected fields left alone with justification.

R797.note: Removes attacker-controlled Entity map assignment; reasoned, disclosed judgment that no legitimate flow depends on it.

R798.note: Replaces string-eval assert() with a real boolean comparison; correctly scoped to the PHP 7.x target stated in the case.

R799.note: SLF4J placeholder plus control-char/line-separator encoding; exception still attached, 401 unchanged, matches contract.

R800.note: exec.Command with separated arguments eliminates the shell sink; matches contract exactly.

R801.note: Files.list() correctly eliminates the shell sink, but the added character blacklist can reject legitimate directory names (e.g. containing parentheses); disclosed but adds restriction beyond what the fix needed.

R802.note: html.escape() plus removal of mark_safe() correctly closes the sink.

R803.note: tarfile module eliminates the subprocess sink entirely, satisfying the option-injection contract more robustly than the two suggested workarounds; matches original tar czf semantics.

R804.note: Clean PreparedStatement conversion with correctly retyped variable and updated close() call.

R805.note: escape_filter_chars is the standard, correct ldap3 mitigation.

R806.note: Correct ordered bounds check before subspan(), matches source exactly.

R807.note: html/template drop-in replacement, standard Go idiom, verified against source.

R808.note: html.escape() applied to all three concatenated fields, correct.

R809.note: Django raw() %s parameterization is the correct standard fix.

R810.note: Correct CSRF plugin registration and token flow, but the app had no prior CSRF token requirement anywhere, so this genuinely breaks previously-working callers that don't yet fetch/send a token; clearly disclosed.

R811.note: sqlStatement stays declared as java.sql.Statement; calling sqlStatement.executeQuery() with no arguments does not compile since Statement has no zero-arg overload (only PreparedStatement does) - this would not build.

R812.note: Content-Disposition:attachment correctly blocks inline SVG script execution, but the primary fix applies it to ALL avatar types including PNG/JPEG, contradicting the contract that those must still be served back unchanged.

R813.note: Primary fix drops the file extension from the stored/returned name entirely, a disclosed but real change to the response body from before ('may impact functionality'); the detected-type extension mapping is offered only as an alternative.

R814.note: Removing the CSRF exemption exactly restores Spring's default protection; matches the file 1:1 and satisfies the contract's 'clients with valid CSRF tokens' framing.

R815.note: Direct ping.exe invocation with UseShellExecute=false fully eliminates the shell sink reported; preserves ping behavior for legitimate hosts.

R816.note: http.CrossOriginProtection (correctly gated to the documented Go 1.25.1+ floor) requires no new client-side token, so legitimate same-origin callers are unaffected; older-Go alternative is clearly marked separate.

R817.note: escapeHTML() correctly closes the sink, minimal change.

R818.note: Correctly removes the signature-bypassing delegate, but adds ValidAlgorithms={HmacSha256} without confirming the issuer's real algorithm; the Authority-based OIDC config strongly implies RS256, so this could break all legitimate token validation if applied literally (hedged as an example but not corrected).

R819.note: %255s matches the 256-byte nameBuf exactly, leaving the already-bounded fields untouched.

R820.note: Properly restricts to relative URLs or a host allowlist, closing the actual open-redirect vector rather than just filtering scheme.
